bull.b: Recurring chemistry purchases can extend revenue beyond initial equipment sales and deepen customer relationships. The eye-health deployment also expanded from handheld systems to environment systems across facilities, illustrating a pathway toward larger, repeatable account value.

Growing backlog and substantial advanced-stage opportunities provide clearer revenue visibility than relying solely on new bookings. If execution continues, these projects can support near-term growth, improve utilization of the installed platform, and create additional opportunities for consumables and services.

Additional regulatory registrations broaden the situations in which TOMI can market and deploy its technology, while new patents may help protect product development. Together, these advances expand the addressable use cases and support longer-term commercial adoption across food safety and international markets.

bear.b: Ongoing operating and free-cash-flow deficits mean growth is not yet self-funded and can require continued access to external capital. Persistent losses also reduce financial resilience, making execution against the pipeline important for moving toward sustainable profitability and preserving operating flexibility.

High leverage relative to equity reduces balance-sheet flexibility while the company remains loss-making. Convertible-note activity can improve reported equity or support compliance, but conversions and lower conversion terms may dilute existing holders and increase dependence on financing actions to fund operations.

Important strategic and commercial opportunities depend on financing and regulatory milestones that are not yet assured. Delays or failure in the merger funding condition or required approvals could postpone product expansion, increase transaction costs, and weaken the timing of expected pipeline conversion.
